title: The Relief List
subtitle: Flood relief reached one lane and not the next; the list is being called rigged
coldOpen: Three days after the flood, relief kits reached Lane 2.
Lane 3, just as wet, got nothing.
A list with names is being passed hand to hand.

briefing.grievance: Families in Lane 3 lost as much as Lane 2 and received nothing. They believe the relief list was written for someone’s voters. They want kits today and the list explained.
knownFacts: Lane 2 received 180 kits on Tuesday; Lane 3 received none.
The survey team marked Lane 3 “pending” because the lane was still flooded on survey day.
A second consignment of 400 kits is at the collectorate warehouse.
unverifiedClaims: A post says a councillor’s relatives got double kits.
A message says Lane 3 was skipped on purpose for the way it voted.
briefing.responsibility: You run the relief operation and the survey office. Kits and fairness both run through you.
briefing.objective: Get Lane 3 its kits today, show how the list was made, and stop the favouritism story from becoming a fight.

rightsMoments.question: A lane says it was skipped for relief because of how it voted. What does equal treatment require of you?

options.text: Apply the same relief criteria to every lane, show how the list was made, and correct any gap promptly.
options.feedback: Correct. Equality is about even-handed criteria and a visible, correctable process.

options.text: Give the complaining lane extra kits to settle the matter.
options.feedback: Extra kits for whoever complains loudest is itself unequal treatment.

options.text: Stop all relief until the accusation is fully investigated.
options.feedback: Halting relief punishes everyone for an unproven claim and deepens the harm.

rightsMoments.principle: Article 14 requires equal treatment under clear criteria. Relief must follow need, with a process people can inspect, and errors must be fixed without punishing anyone.
rightsMoments.why: The survey had marked the lane “pending” because of water; showing the sheet and sending the trucks answered the accusation better than any inquiry.

simple.question: A lane says it was skipped for help because of how it voted. What is fair?

options.a: Use the same rules for every lane, show how the list was made, fix gaps fast.
options.b: Give the complaining lane extra kits.
options.c: Stop all help until the complaint is investigated.

feedback.a: Yes! Same rules, open process, quick fixes.
feedback.b: No. Extra for whoever shouts loudest is unfair too.
feedback.c: Stopping help punishes everyone for an unproven claim.

simple.principle: Everyone gets help by the same rules. Show how the list was made and fix mistakes fast.
simple.why: The lane was marked “pending” because of water. Showing the sheet and sending trucks answered it.
